linux.openwireshark.9_0.instruction:
Configure the OpenWireshark workspace to the Retail Incident Review profile and load the retail_mix.pcapng capture from the recent files list. The session must conclude with the OpenWireshark brand title selected in the top-left corner, the interface list showing the any card selected, and the packet list displaying HTTP and TCP records filtered by tcp.port == 80.

The DNS bench.local saved filter view must expose the first DNS packet with the Domain Name System group expanded to show the Queries entry, the Internet Protocol group displaying source and destination addresses, and the User Datagram Protocol group showing DNS port information. The packet bytes area for this view must have the Hex tab selected after the ASCII tab has been viewed. The statistics panel must reflect the Conversations button selected after the Endpoints button, and the Expert Information dialog must be closed with the EXPERT list cleared to empty.

The Checkout HTTP saved filter view must expose the GET /checkout HTTP/1.1 packet with the Hypertext Transfer Protocol group selected to display the Host and User-Agent entries. The packet bytes area for this view must have the Bits tab selected after the ASCII tab has been viewed. The statistics panel must reflect the IO Graph button selected after the Protocol Hierarchy button, and the Decode As dialog must be closed.

The HTTP/1.1 200 OK packet within the Checkout HTTP view must expose the Hypertext Transfer Protocol group displaying the Content-Type and Content-Length entries. The packet bytes area for this view must have the ASCII tab selected, and the Coloring Rules dialog must be closed.

The Initial SYN saved filter view must expose the first TCP SYN packet with the Transmission Control Protocol group selected to display the Flags entry. The packet bytes area for this view must have the ASCII tab selected after the Hex tab has been viewed. The statistics panel must reflect the Endpoints button selected after the Conversations button, and the Expert Information dialog must be closed.

The tcp.port == 80 display filter must be applied to the packet list, exposing the POST /api/cart/confirm packet with the Hypertext Transfer Protocol group selected to display the JavaScript Object Notation request payload. The packet bytes area for this view must have the ASCII tab selected. The statistics panel must reflect the IO Graph button selected after the Protocol Hierarchy button.

The toolbar must reflect the Zoom Out button selected after the Zoom In button, and the Colorize button selected. The Preferences dialog must be closed.

linux.openwireshark.9_1.instruction:
Review the `retail_mix.pcapng` capture in OpenWireshark using the `Retail Incident Review` profile, covering DNS, checkout HTTP, TCP handshake and error packets, link health, and capture settings. The DNS review should apply `DNS bench.local`, inspect the `Standard query` packet in `ASCII` and `Hex`, and include the `Endpoints`, `Protocol Hierarchy`, `IO Graph`, and `Expert Information` views with `NOTE - Packet 21` selected. The checkout review should apply `Checkout HTTP` to inspect `GET /checkout HTTP/1.1` in `Bits` and follow its TCP stream before closing that view. Under `Port 80`, inspect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` in `ASCII` and `POST /api/cart/confirm` in `Hex`; include the `Conversations` and `IO Graph` statistics views and an opened, then dismissed, `Export Specified Packets` dialog.

Include a `Zoom In` pass and apply the display filter `http`. The packet search should find `checkout` and use both `Back` and `Forward` navigation before the filter is cleared. Under the saved `Initial SYN` filter, inspect `53120 -> 80 [SYN]` in `Bits`, use `Next Packet`, and inspect `80 -> 53120 [SYN, ACK]`; the `Decode As` dialog should be viewed and dismissed. Apply `tcp.flags.ack == 1` to inspect `53120 -> 80 [ACK]`, then clear the filter. Under `Errors and warnings`, inspect `WARNING - Packet 20` and `ERROR - Packet 26` and dismiss the `Coloring Rules` dialog after reviewing it. Under `Link health`, inspect the first `ARP` packet in `ASCII` and the `Endpoints` statistics view. The capture interface review should include `eth0` followed by `any`, with `tcp port 80` entered as the capture filter in the `Options` dialog before it is closed. Review `Supported Filters` in Help and dismiss that panel with `Esc`. Finish with `Zoom Out` in the toolbar.

linux.openwireshark.9_2.instruction:
Configure OpenWireshark to process three capture files with specific filters, packet selections, view states, and dialog interactions.

For the dns_bench_lookup.pcapng capture file loaded from the recent files list under the DNS Triage profile, apply the saved filter DNS bench.local. Select the packet row labeled Standard query 0x7f21 and display its payload using the ASCII view in the packet bytes panel. Open the Protocol Hierarchy, Endpoints, and Expert Information statistics views, and within the expert panel select the entry labeled NOTE - Packet 21. Clear the current display filter, enter dns.qry.name into the filter field, and apply it. Select the packet row labeled Standard query response and switch the packet bytes panel to the Hex view.

For the retail_mix.pcapng capture file loaded from the recent files list, apply the saved filter Checkout HTTP. Select the packet row labeled GET /checkout HTTP/1.1, open the Analyze menu, and choose Follow TCP Stream; close the resulting TCP stream window with the Esc key. Apply the saved filter Port 80, select the packet row labeled HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted, and switch the packet bytes panel to the Bits view. Open the Conversations statistics view and switch the statistics panel to the IO Graph chart. Open the Export Specified Packets dialog and close it with the Esc key. Use the Find tool to search for cart, then use the Back and Forward navigation buttons to move through the search results.

Apply the saved filter Initial SYN and select the packet row labeled 53144 -> 8080 [SYN]. Open the Go menu and choose Next Packet, then select the packet row labeled [TCP Retransmission]. Open the Decode As dialog and close it with the Esc key. Enter tcp.port == 8080 into the filter field and apply it, then select the packet row labeled 8080 -> 53144 [RST, ACK]. Apply the saved filter Errors and warnings, and in the expert panel select the entries labeled WARNING - Packet 25 and ERROR - Packet 26. Open the Coloring Rules dialog and close it with the Esc key.

Apply the saved filter Local host and select the packet row for the local host 10.10.0.2, then switch the packet bytes panel to the ASCII view. Open the Endpoints statistics view. Apply the saved filter Link health, select the first ARP link packet row, and switch the packet bytes panel to the Hex view. In the interface list, select lo, then eth0, and finally any. Open the capture Options dialog, enter udp port 53 into the Capture filter field, and close the dialog. Open the View menu and choose Colorize Packet List, then use the Zoom Out toolbar button. Open the Help menu, choose Supported Filters, and close the help panel with the Esc key.

linux.openzotero.blur_gate_vision_review.instruction:
Configure the OpenZotero item "Edges Before Embeddings: A Confidence-Aware Blur Gate for Vision-Language Pipelines" and its duplicate within the cs.CV tag context to reflect a completed review workflow, resulting in two distinct item records with specific statuses, notes, tags, and collection assignments.

The primary item, identified by the search term "Blur Gate" within the cs.CV tag, must have its Status set to "In Review" on the Info tab. Its existing note content must be entirely replaced with the text "Review blur gate confidence before vision pipeline meeting." and saved. The tag "vision-review" must be added to this item. The attachment named "2606.25838 Edges Before Embeddings_ A Confidence-Aware Blur Gate for Vision-Language Pipelines.pdf" must be selected in the Attachments tab. This item must be assigned to a new collection named "Vision Papers" created under "My Library".

A duplicate of the primary item must be created and located within the "Vision Papers" collection under the Special section. This duplicated item must have its Status changed to "Archived" on the Info tab. In its Notes tab, the text "Blur gate comparison retained" must be appended on a new line at the end of the existing note text and saved. The tag "vision-review" must also be added to this duplicated item.

The primary "Edges Before Embeddings" item must be further updated by appending the text "Confidence threshold checked" on a new line at the end of its note text and saving the note. The tag "blur-gate-reviewed" must be added to this primary item. A new collection named "Blur Gate Vision Review" must be created. The final state must include the "Vision Papers" and "Blur Gate Vision Review" collections, the primary item with status "In Review" and tags "vision-review" and "blur-gate-reviewed", and the duplicated item with status "Archived" and tag "vision-review", with all specified note modifications saved.

linux.openzotero.review_queue_duplicate_.instruction: Create a new collection named Review Queue in OpenZotero with My Library as its parent, containing a Report item titled Benchmark Recovery Notes and its duplicate, Benchmark Recovery Notes (Copy). The original item must have creators Maya Chen and Leo Park, the year 2026, the abstract Short notes about recovery checks for agent benchmarks, and the tags benchmark, recovery, and reliability. Its status must be set to In Review, and it must contain a note with the text Review failure modes before citation. The duplicate item, titled Benchmark Recovery Notes (Copy), must have its status set to Cited and must contain a note with the text Keep copy for duplicate review, replacing any inherited note content. The final state of the application must display the contents of the Review Queue collection in the left-hand library panel.

linux.openzotero.toolbenchx_reliability_.instruction: Update the OpenZotero library to reflect the review status of the ToolBench-X paper and the creation of a companion report item. The item titled "Beyond Function Calling: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents under Tool-Environment Unreliability" must have its status set to "In Review" and include a tag named "tool-reliability". The notes section for this item must contain only the exact string "ToolBench-X reliability hazards reviewed." A new collection named "Agent Reliability Review" must exist with "My Library" as its parent, and the "Beyond Function Calling: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents under Tool-Environment Unreliability" item must be assigned to this collection. A new item titled "Tool Hazard Reading Log" must be created with the creator set to "Maya Chen", the type set to "Report", and the year set to "2026". This new item must be assigned to the "Agent Reliability Review" collection, tagged with "tool-reliability" and "notes", and have the abstract field containing the text "Companion log for ToolBench-X reliability reading." The final state of the library must reflect these specific changes to the existing paper and the creation of the new report item, without adding, deleting, or modifying any other items. OpenZotero is a web app: open it from the OpenZotero icon in the webpage folder on the desktop, which opens it in Chrome.

linux.thunderbird.6_4_mail_filter.instruction: In Thunderbird Mail, create two new folders and two subject-based message filters under Local Folders. Local Folders must contain new folders named `BillsDesk64` and `TripsDesk64`. The Local Folders message filters must include an enabled filter named `Bill64Route` and an enabled filter named `Travel64Route`, each with the Archiving and Periodically, every 10 minutes triggers checked and set to Match any of the following. Bill64Route must use the conditions Subject contains `invoice64` and Subject contains `receipt64` with the action Move Message to Local Folders > `BillsDesk64`. Travel64Route must use the conditions Subject contains `booking64` and Subject contains `checkin64` with the action Move Message to Local Folders > `TripsDesk64`. Both filters must be saved so they persist in the Local Folders filter rules, and finally, with the filter list narrowed by the search text `64`, Bill64Route must be run once with Run Now on the `BillsDesk64` folder.

linux.thunderbird.calendar.thunderbird2_.instruction: In Thunderbird's Calendar, dismiss any popup that appears (without logging out), move to the week of July 6 to July 10, 2026, and create a set of nine events that all persist in the local calendar, each title appearing exactly once. "Kickoff Alignment" must be on July 6, 2026 from 09:20 to 10:00. "Requirements Freeze" must be on July 6, 2026 from 13:10 to 13:55 with a single reminder 15 minutes before. "Prototype Review" must be on July 7, 2026 from 10:30 to 11:15. "Data Migration Check" must be on July 8, 2026 from 08:45 to 09:30 with a reminder 15 minutes before. "Stakeholder Demo Prep" must be on July 8, 2026 from 15:00 to 15:50. "Security Review Window" must be on July 9, 2026 from 11:40 to 12:20 with a reminder 30 minutes before. "Weekly Delivery Sync" must be on July 10, 2026 from 09:00 to 09:35, repeating every week (Weekly), with a reminder 30 minutes before. "Launch Decision Brief" must be on July 10, 2026 from 16:15 to 17:00; it is first saved without a description and then edited so that its description is exactly "Decision owners confirmed". "Release Readiness" must be on July 9, 2026 from 14:00 to 14:40 with a reminder 15 minutes before and the description "Review launch blockers". Events without a stated reminder, repeat rule, or description should keep none, and every event must be saved with Save and Close so the week plan retains the release events and their descriptions.

linux.thunderbird.mail.thunderbird3_revi.instruction: In Thunderbird, produce two related drafts addressed to `assistant@outlook.com` in the Local Folders `Drafts` folder: an original draft and a revised copy of it. The original draft, composed from the `anonym-x2024@outlook.com` account, must have the subject `Support triage check` and a body of exactly two lines, `Owner:Alex` and `Status:Draft only`; it must be saved and kept unchanged, remaining unread and not starred. The revised draft must be created from the original with Edit As New Message (so the original is preserved) and, in its final saved form, must have the subject `Support triage check - final` and a body of exactly these lines in order: `Owner:Alex`, `Status:Draft only`, `Follow-up:pending`, `Ready for review`, `Priority:high`, and `Next review:Monday`. The copy is built up in stages that are each saved: first with the added line `Follow-up:pending`, then with ` - final` appended to the subject and the line `Ready for review`, and finally with `Priority:high` and `Next review:Monday` appended at the end of the body. In the final state, the Drafts folder must contain exactly one draft with each subject, and the `Support triage check - final` draft must be marked as read and starred.

linux.thunderbird.qa66_mail_folder_searc.instruction: In Thunderbird Mail, which is already available in the snap_2 VM state, create a new local folder and a new calendar event while working through the Local Folders tools, leaving the seeded data intact. Local Folders must stay expanded, and its existing folders Trash, Attachments - Images PDFs, Bills, Inbox History, Personal - Friends Family, Promotions Receipts, Travel Events Services, and Work - Bench Project must remain in place. Message searches run from Local Folders with the Search Messages window (for `travel`, `bills`, a From condition of `qa66`, and an added Subject condition of `receipt`) are only transient and must leave no lasting changes, and the Search Messages window must be closed afterwards. A filter draft named `qa66 filter` may be started in the Message Filters dialog but must be cancelled so that no such filter is saved, and the Message Filters window must be closed. Local Folders must contain a new folder named `qa66box`. In the right-side Events panel, which shows seeded events such as Cabin weekend packing, Drive to cabin, and Return from cabin, a new event titled `qa66 event` must be created and saved with Save and Close so that it is stored in the Thunderbird calendar. Finish with Local Folders selected in the folder tree and the right Events panel still visible.

linux.thunderbird_calendar.5_5_goal5_ubu.instruction: In Thunderbird's Calendar, close the reminder popup and create two events in the local calendar, then leave the calendar filtered to the second one. The first event must be titled `Gate714` (replacing any default title text), with Location `Room214`, Category Appointment, a start of 14/7/2026 at 09:40 and an end of 14/7/2026 at 10:25, a reminder 15 minutes before, and the description `gate prep`, saved with Save and Close. Between the two events, the event list filter must be changed from Events in the Next 7 Days to All Events and `Gate714` searched for. The second event must be titled `Ops716` (replacing any default title text), with Location `Bridge5`, Category Business, a start of 16/7/2026 at 13:10 and an end of 16/7/2026 at 14:00, repeating Weekly, a reminder 30 minutes before, and the description `ops handoff`, saved with Save and Close. Finish with the calendar in Week view and the calendar search text replaced by `Ops716`.

linux.thunderbird_calendar.goal6_6_5.instruction: In Thunderbird's Calendar, create two events in the local calendar and finish with the second one selected in the event search results. The first event must be titled `QA Gate 714`, with Location `Room 214`, Category Appointment, a start of 14/7/2026 at 09:40 and an end of 14/7/2026 at 10:25, a reminder 15 minutes before, the description `gate prep`, and Privacy set to Private Event, saved with Save and Close. The second event must be titled `Ops Sync 716`, with Location `Bridge 5`, Category Work, a start of 16/7/2026 at 13:10 and an end of 16/7/2026 at 14:00, repeating Weekly, a reminder 30 minutes before, the description `ops handoff`, the attendee `ops@local.test` invited, and the Disallow counter option enabled, saved with Save and Close. Finish in Week view with the event search filter set to All Events and the search text `Ops Sync`, and with `Ops Sync 716` selected in the resulting event list.

linux.thunderbird_calendar.ops_schedule_.instruction: In Thunderbird's Calendar, dismiss any popup without changing account settings or logging out, and build a nine-event operations schedule spanning June 29 to July 31, 2026, with every event saved via Save and Close in the local calendar (America/New_York time). "Ops Intake Review" must be on June 29, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 9:30 AM, and "Vendor Contract Check" on June 29, 2026 from 2:15 AM to 3:00 AM. "Inventory Sync" must be on June 30, 2026 from 10:45 AM to 11:30 AM with a reminder 15 minutes before the start. "Regional Staffing Check" must be on July 1, 2026 from 1:00 AM to 2:00 AM. "Compliance Packet Review" must be on July 2, 2026 from 8:30 AM to 9:15 AM with a reminder 15 minutes before, and "Customer Escalation Window" on July 2, 2026 from 3:30 AM to 4:00 AM. "Weekly Operations Pulse" must be on Friday, July 3, 2026 from 11:00 AM to 11:45 AM, repeating either weekly or every weekday, with a reminder 30 minutes before. After returning to the calendar and moving to the week of July 6 to July 10, 2026, "Kickoff Alignment" must be created on July 6, 2026 from 09:20 to 10:00 and saved before the final event is created. Finally, a new event whose default title text is fully replaced by "Final Review" must be on July 31, 2026 from 16:00 to 16:30 with a reminder 15 minutes before and the description `qa75`.

macos.deltachat.atlas_access_fixes.instruction: Populate the DeltaChat account on macOS with the specified audit records, group configurations, and message sequences. The Saved Messages chat must contain the exact text of the message from Nora QA that includes the search term nav_bar_search with the suffix " | audit source" appended to the end, followed by the messages "Owner Maya Friday", "Keys before color", "Review scope locked", and "Atlas matrix ready" in that exact order, with "Atlas matrix ready" remaining the latest message in that chat. A new group named "Atlas Access" must be created and populated with the message "Owner Maya Friday", the exact text of the message from Alice Design that includes the search term design_search_anchor with the suffix " | visual source" appended to the end, and the messages "Keyboard pass first" and "Contrast pass next" in that exact order, concluding with the exact text of the "Atlas matrix ready" message from Saved Messages with the suffix " | final index" appended to the end, making "Atlas matrix ready | final index" the latest message in that chat. A new group named "Atlas Fixes" must be created and populated with the exact text of the message from Bob Ops that includes the search term ops_launch_green with the suffix " | release gate" appended to the end, followed by the messages "Release after review" and "Maya owns closure" in that exact order, and finally the messages "Keyboard proof filed" and "Contrast proof filed" in that exact order, with "Contrast proof filed" being the latest message in that chat. The task is complete when the Atlas Fixes chat is the active view and all specified messages exist in the correct order within their respective chats.

macos.deltachat.harbor_migration_brief.instruction:
Create a new DeltaChat group named Harbor Control and populate it with the migration sequence, then build a second group named Harbor Review that references the saved evidence, leaving the application in the Harbor Control conversation with all specified messages and attachments present.

Harbor Control must contain six self-sent text messages in this exact order: Freeze at 08:30, Owner is Riley, Database copy first, API switch second, Migration brief done, and Client notice queued. The message Client notice queued must be the latest self-sent text in Harbor Control.

Saved Messages must contain the text Freeze at 08:30 | harbor record, which is the full text of the Freeze at 08:30 message from Harbor Control with the suffix " | harbor record" appended. Saved Messages must also contain the full text of the message from Bob Ops that contains the term ops_launch_green, with the suffix " | backend proof" appended to the end of that pasted text. Saved Messages must contain a self-sent attachment of the file Round1_Ops.txt from the Documents folder, and a self-sent attachment of the file Round2_Design.txt from the Documents folder, with Round2_Design.txt appearing after Round1_Ops.txt in the conversation.

Harbor Review must contain the full text of the message in Saved Messages that contains the phrase backend proof, with the suffix " | review copy" appended to the end of that pasted text. Harbor Review must also contain the full text of the message from Nora QA that contains the term nav_bar_search, with the suffix " | frontend proof" appended to the end of that pasted text. Harbor Review must contain the text message Both gates reviewed, which must be the latest self-sent text in Harbor Review.

macos.deltachat.nova_command_event_clear.instruction:
Compile the Nova Command event clearance record in DeltaChat by forwarding three specific source messages to Saved Messages with designated suffixes, attaching two operational files, posting three status updates, and establishing a new group chat populated with the final clearance sequence.

The Saved Messages chat must contain three forwarded text messages in this order: the exact text of the message from Nora QA containing the search term nav_bar_search with the suffix " | mobile proof" appended, the exact text of the message from Bob Ops containing the search term ops_launch_green with the suffix " | venue gate" appended, and the exact text of the message from Alice Design containing the search term design_search_anchor with the suffix " | guest design" appended. Following these three messages, the file Round1_Ops.txt from the Documents folder must be attached and sent, immediately followed by the attachment and sending of the file Round2_Design.txt from the Documents folder. After the attachments, three separate text messages must appear in Saved Messages in this exact order: "Event opens 18:00", "Doors check at 17", and "Owner is Morgan".

A new group named "Nova Command" must be created and populated with seven text messages in this exact order: the exact text "Event opens 18:00" with the suffix " | command time" appended, followed by "Doors check at 17", "Owner is Morgan", "Mobile proof linked", "Venue gate linked", "Guest design linked", and "Nova event cleared".

The task is complete when the Nova Command group is the active view, the Saved Messages chat ends with "Owner is Morgan" as the latest self-sent text, and the Nova Command chat ends with "Nova event cleared" as the latest message.

macos.deltachat.orion_launch_handoff.instruction: Populate the DeltaChat account on macOS with four specific chat threads containing exact self-message sequences. The Saved Messages chat must contain four self-messages in this order: “Orion launch brief”, “Cutover at 21:00”, “Rollback owner set”, and “Orion archive ready”, with “Orion archive ready” as the most recent entry. A new group named “Orion Launch” must be created and populated with three self-messages in this order: “Orion launch brief | owner plan”, “Rollback owner set | launch record”, and “Archive link shared”, with “Archive link shared” as the most recent entry. A new group named “Orion Ops” must be created and populated with two self-messages in this order: the exact full text of the message from Bob Ops containing the search token “ops_launch_green” followed by the suffix “ | gate green”, and the exact full text of the message from Nora QA containing the search token “nav_bar_search” followed by the suffix “ | nav checked”, preserving the complete source text for both with only the specified suffixes appended. A new group named “Orion Handoff” must be created and populated with five self-messages in this order: “Launch window fixed”, “Ops gate captured”, “Nav audit captured”, “Owner handoff ready”, and “Archive handoff set”, with “Archive handoff set” as the most recent entry. All messages must be sent by the logged-in account itself, and the final state must reflect these exact message sequences in each of the four chats.

macos.openbank.macos1_june_home_bills_tr.instruction: Sign in to the OpenBank application with the username jordan and the password vault2026 to access Jordan Lee's account, where three scheduled bill payments and one scheduled transfer must be recorded on the June home bills page and in the Transfers section. The first scheduled bill payment is for City Utilities, drawn from the Rainy Day Savings account ending in 9140, for an amount of 92.35, scheduled for 2026-06-02, with the memo June utilities. The second scheduled bill payment is for Northstar Internet, drawn from the Everyday Checking account ending in 2381, for an amount of 72.00, scheduled for 2026-06-06, with the memo June internet. The third scheduled bill payment is for the OpenBank Rewards Card, drawn from the Rainy Day Savings account ending in 9140, for an amount of 120.00, scheduled for 2026-06-10, with the memo Card payment. The scheduled transfer is to Avery Brooks for a rent share, drawn from the Rainy Day Savings account ending in 9140, for an amount of 14.35, scheduled for 2026-06-18, with the memo Rent share. This document must be saved as a UTF-8 plain text file named June-Home.txt to the Desktop. The task is complete when the three bill payments and the Avery Brooks transfer are recorded as scheduled in the account, the file June-Home.txt exists on the Desktop with the specified content, and the TextEdit application is the active foreground window.

macos.openbank.macos1_reserve_plan_bills.instruction:
Sign in to OpenBank with the username jordan and the password vault2026 to access Jordan Lee’s account, where two scheduled bill payments and two scheduled transfers must be created, followed by a summary text file saved to the Desktop.

The Pay & transfer area must contain two scheduled bill payments for June 2026. The first payment is for City Utilities, paid from the Rainy Day Savings account ending in 9140, for an amount of 92.35, scheduled for 2026-06-02, with the memo June utilities. The second payment is for Northstar Internet, paid from the Everyday Checking account ending in 2381, for an amount of 72.00, scheduled for 2026-06-06, with the memo June internet. Both bill payments must be saved as Scheduled.

The second transfer moves 70.30 from the Everyday Checking account ending in 2381 to the Rainy Day Savings account, scheduled for 2026-06-26, with the memo Reserve restore. macos.openbank.macos1_studio_recipients_.instruction:
Sign in to OpenBank with the username jordan and the password vault2026 to access Jordan Lee's account, and create two new recipients, submit two scheduled transfers, leave one supplier allocation form populated but unsubmitted, and save a specific text file to the Desktop.

The first recipient record must be named Sofia Reed with the nickname Studio share, bank Harbor Community, routing number 026009593, and account number 0000007318. The second recipient record must be named Ethan Cole with the nickname Design refund, bank Civic Credit Union, routing number 021000021, and account number 0000004826. In the supplier allocation area, the source account must be set to Rainy Day Savings ...9140 and the destination recipient must be set to Maya Patel, but this form must not be submitted.

At completion, the Studio-Pay.txt file must exist on the Desktop, TextEdit must be the foreground application displaying the saved document, and the OpenBank session must remain logged in as Jordan Lee without signing out.

macos.openbank.macos1_travel_hold_paymen.instruction: Sign in to the OpenBank application as Jordan Lee using the username jordan and the password vault2026, and maintain this active session throughout the workflow. The Account activity page must reflect a search filtered for the OpenBank Rewards Card ending in 7712, the Travel category, and the Pending status, with the details for the Hotel Meridian card hold transaction opened. Two scheduled transfers must be submitted: one for 46.90 from Rainy Day Savings ending in 9140 to Ethan Cole dated 2026-06-24 with the memo Trip refund, and a second for 31.45 from Everyday Checking ending in 2381 to Avery Brooks dated 2026-06-21 with the memo Travel split. A new plain text document in TextEdit must contain the lines TYPE=CARD HOLD, AMOUNT=120.00, and STATUS=PENDING, saved as Travel-Hold.txt to the Desktop. macos.opendriver.driver_docs_support_pay.instruction: Sign in to the OpenDriver application using the Driver login page with the email driver@example.com and the password Password123! to access the driver workspace for Maya Rodriguez. The driver profile in the Account section must be updated so that the License number is NY-DL-100492, the Vehicle make is Tesla, the Vehicle model is Model Y, the Plate is 8XJR214, and the Color is Pearl white, with the changes saved for review. The Driver documents area must contain two submitted records: a Driver license document with the Document ID DL-2026-100492 and an Expires at date of 2027-12-31, and an Insurance document with the Document ID INS-2026-3091 and an Expires at date of 2028-06-30. A new support ticket in the Support section must be created with the exact message Rider ID question. The Money section must include a submitted payout request for an Amount of 75.00 with the Note Fuel reimbursement. A new plain-text document in TextEdit must contain exactly three lines: the first line PAYOUT=75.00, the second line DOCS=2, and the third line PLATE=8XJR214, and this file must be saved to the Desktop with the filename Driver-Docs.txt. The task is complete when the OpenDriver session remains signed in as Maya Rodriguez with all profile, document, support, and payout records persisted, the file Driver-Docs.txt exists on the Desktop with the specified contents, and TextEdit is the foreground application.

macos.opendriver.driver_weekly_closeout_.instruction:
Sign in to the OpenDriver application using the Driver role with the email driver@example.com and the password Password123! to enter the Maya Rodriguez driver workspace, where a new request generated from the Work area must be accepted and confirmed as active in the trip panel. The Money area must contain two separate payout requests: one with an amount of 120.00 and a note of Weekly payout, and a second with an amount of 45.00 and a note of Trip reserve. ROLE=DRIVER
PAYOUTS=165.00
DOC=INS-2026-2048
This file must be saved to the Desktop with the filename Driver-Week.txt, with TextEdit remaining the foreground application and the driver session still active in OpenDriver at completion.

macos.opendriver.rider_commute_fare_revi.instruction:
Sign in to the OpenDriver rider application with the email rider@example.com and the password Password123! to access the account for Riley Rider, and request a standard RideX commute ride to Downtown Palo Alto, CA, paying with the Visa ending in 4242 and applying the promo code COMMUTE15 so that the ride is submitted with a positive discount and the promo code is recorded as used.

Update the rider profile so that the name is exactly Riley Commute and the phone number is exactly 6505550194, and save these changes. In the Wallet area, set the Mastercard ending in 9001 as the active default payment method. Interact with the Coupons area by copying the WELCOME20 coupon, and interact with the Saved places area by opening the Home — Downtown Palo Alto saved place. Review the History and Receipt information for the commute ride, including the Payment and Total areas.

Open TextEdit and create a new plain-text document containing exactly three lines in this order: ROUTE=DOWNTOWN, RIDE=RIDEX, and TICKET=FARE OPEN. Save this document as Commute-Fare.txt on the Desktop. When the task is complete, TextEdit must remain the foreground application, the rider must remain signed in, and the OpenDriver session must not be logged out.

macos.opendriver.rider_priority_lost_tex.instruction: Sign in to the OpenDriver rider application using the email rider@example.com and the password Password123! to access the account for Riley Rider, and request a Priority pickup ride from University Avenue to Downtown Palo Alto, CA, using the Visa ending in 4242 as the payment method. The Safety section must contain two support tickets, both categorized as lost item: the first with the message exactly Lost blue umbrella. and a reply containing exactly Found it, thank you., and the second with the message exactly Bag tag missing and a reply containing exactly Tag details sent. The account profile must reflect the phone number 6505550172, and the Wallet section must have the Mastercard ending in 9001 set as the active default payment method. The Ride page must display the destination pre-filled from the saved place named Work. A new plain text document in the TextEdit application must contain the three lines RIDE=PRIORITY, ITEM=BLUE UMBRELLA, and TICKET=LOST OPEN, each on its own separate line, and be saved as a UTF-8 plain text file named Priority-Lost.txt to the Desktop.

macos.opennote.macos1_canal_train_walk_l.instruction: Produce a completed OpenNote session under the Lina Park account where the Travel post “What changed after I tried train day trip” is liked, saved, and commented with the exact text `Train route noted`, and the author of that post is followed. Lina Park’s profile must display `rail photo planner` as the Role and `Film walks by train` as the Bio. The Recommended feed post “A small note on coastal coffee stop and ticket screenshot” must be liked, saved, and commented with the exact text `Cafe stop mapped`, while the author of this specific post remains unfollowed. A new published note titled `Canal Train Walk` with the body `Meet at East Station` must exist, categorized as Travel, located at `East Station`, tagged with `train,canal`, and featuring an enabled text cover. The cart must contain 2 Pork Dumplings and 2 Beef Chow Fun from Dumpling Room No. 20 San Jose CA, reflecting a Subtotal of $35.50. With the WELCOME12 coupon applied, the Discount must be -$12, the Delivery fee $2.24, the Service fee $1.80, and the final Total $27.54, without placing the order or clearing the cart.

The Customer Orders view must locate order OF-2001 to verify its date, delivery address, courier, Delivered status, order amount, the two items with their quantities, and the delivery notes, and find order OF-2009 to check its date, delivery address, courier, Delivered status, order amount, item details, and order notes. Order OF-2017 must be located in the Orders list to confirm its status is Delivered, without initiating any Reorder actions. The Customer Wallet view must confirm the Profile Role is Customer and the Wallet balance is displayed, while the Coupons area must verify that the WELCOME12 coupon rule is $12 off orders over $30, without resetting the local OpenFood state or claiming any coupons. The Customer Support view must locate ticket T-901 to confirm it is associated with OF-2026 and has a Resolved status, while reviewing the issue description and admin reply, and find ticket T-909 to confirm it shows No order and a Resolved status, without filling out or submitting the New support ticket form.

The Merchant view must verify that Dumpling Room No. 20 is Open with its first three menu items marked as Available, and that Santana Row Banh Mi Market is Open and all its displayed items are Available, without marking any restaurant as closed or changing the availability of any items. The Courier view must review the Pickup, Dropoff, Status, and Payout for couriers D-331 and D-332, and check D-333 to confirm its status is Needs courier and note its Payout, without accepting any routes or proceeding to the next step.

The Admin view must review the High, Medium, and Low Admin alerts and check the Users section for the Customer, Merchant, Courier, and Admin roles. The final state must be positioned at the All orders section with the first two order cards visible, without initiating Reorder or Advance status actions for any orders.

windows.opennavigation.googleplex_drive_.instruction: In the OpenNavigation application, execute a sequence of route planning operations for multiple destinations, ensuring that the final state of the interface displays the driving route to Googleplex. Both a driving route (with "Leave now" departure) and a walking route must be generated for "Stanford University" from the "Saved" section. A driving route (with "Leave now" departure) and a walking route must be generated for "Googleplex" from the "Recent" section. A driving route (with "Leave now" departure) and a walking route must be generated for "Meta Headquarters" from the "Recent" section. Both a driving route (with "Leave now" departure) and a walking route must be generated for "Mountain View Transit Center" from the "Recent" section. A driving route must be generated for "Googleplex" from the "Recent" section. A walking route must be generated for "Meta Headquarters" from the "Recent" section. A driving route must be generated for "Stanford University" from the "Saved" section. A walking route with the departure time set to "Leave now" must be generated for "Mountain View Transit Center" (selected from search results for "Central Station"). A walking route must be generated for "Meta Headquarters" from the "Recent" section. Lastly, a driving route must be generated for "Googleplex" from the "Recent" section, leaving this driving route to Googleplex as the final visible result in the application.

windows.opennavigation.meta_googleplex_m.instruction: In the OpenNavigation application, generate a sequence of routes and a final multi-stop itinerary ending with a specific saved place configuration. The initial route must be a walking path from the current location to Mountain View Transit Center, which is identified by searching for "Central Station" and selecting that specific result from the list, with the departure time set to Leave now. Following this, generate three consecutive driving routes from the current location to Googleplex, Meta Headquarters, and Mountain View Transit Center in that exact order, each with the departure time set to Leave now. Subsequently, generate a chain of four connected routes: a driving route from Mountain View Transit Center to Stanford University, a walking route from Stanford University to Googleplex, a driving route from Googleplex to Meta Headquarters, and a walking route from Meta Headquarters to Mountain View Transit Center, all with the departure time set to Leave now. The final deliverable is a driving route from the current location to Stanford University, selected from the Saved section, with the departure time setting changed to Other time. This final route must include two waypoints inserted in the following order: Googleplex between the origin and the destination, and Meta Headquarters between Googleplex and Stanford University. The task is complete only when this final route, passing through Googleplex and then Meta Headquarters before reaching Stanford University, is visibly rendered with the Drive mode and Other time setting.

windows.opennavigation.repaired_multisto.instruction:
Generate a sequence of thirteen route plans in the OpenNavigation application, ensuring each plan is submitted with the correct origin, destination, travel mode, and departure time setting. The first three routes must originate from Current location and terminate at Mountain View Transit Center (identified by searching for "Central Station" and selecting the result), Stanford University (selected from the Saved section), and Meta Headquarters (selected from the Recent section), using Walk, Drive, and Walk modes respectively. The fourth route must originate from Current location and terminate at Googleplex (selected from the Recent section) using Drive mode.

The subsequent routes modify the active Directions panel. The fifth route must run from Googleplex to Stanford University in Walk mode. The sixth route must run from Googleplex to Meta Headquarters in Walk mode. The seventh route must run from Meta Headquarters to Mountain View Transit Center (identified by searching for "Central Station") in Drive mode. The eighth route must reset the origin to Current location and terminate at Mountain View Transit Center in Walk mode.

The final five routes must originate from Mountain View Transit Center. The ninth route must terminate at Meta Headquarters in Drive mode with the "Other time" departure setting. The tenth route must terminate at Stanford University in Walk mode with the "Leave now" departure setting. The eleventh route must terminate at Stanford University in Bike mode with the "Other time" departure setting. The twelfth and thirteenth routes must both terminate at Stanford University in Drive mode with the "Leave now" departure setting; the thirteenth route must include two waypoints in the exact order of Googleplex followed by Meta Headquarters, creating a four-point driving route from Mountain View Transit Center via Googleplex and Meta Headquarters to Stanford University. The OpenNavigation route controls must remain visible in the foreground upon completion.

windows.opennavigation.stanford_meta_mul.instruction: Open the OpenNavigation application and configure a series of multi-stop routes to conclude with a visible Drive route from Current location to Meta Headquarters via Stanford University. The initial set of route artifacts must include Drive, Walk, Bike, and Transit options for the path from Current location to Stanford University, followed by a second set of Transit, Bike, Walk, and Drive options for the path from Meta Headquarters to Stanford University. A third set of Walk, Bike, Transit, and Drive routes must be generated for the path from Meta Headquarters to Googleplex. Subsequently, a three-point route sequence from Meta Headquarters to Googleplex via Stanford University must have Transit, Bike, Walk, and Drive routes generated. This sequence must then be modified to originate from Current location, requiring Walk, Bike, Transit, and Drive routes for the path from Current location to Googleplex via Stanford University. The destination of this three-point route must then be changed to Meta Headquarters, necessitating Walk, Bike, Transit, and Drive routes for the path from Current location to Meta Headquarters via Stanford University. The intermediate stop must be swapped to Googleplex, resulting in a route from Current location to Meta Headquarters via Googleplex, for which Transit, Bike, Walk, and Drive routes must be generated. The origin of this sequence must then be changed to Stanford University, requiring Walk, Bike, Transit, and Drive routes for the path from Stanford University to Meta Headquarters via Googleplex. The origin must be reverted to Current location, generating Drive, Transit, Walk, and Bike routes for the path from Current location to Meta Headquarters via Googleplex. The intermediate stop must be restored to Stanford University, creating the final configuration of Current location to Meta Headquarters via Stanford University, for which Walk, Bike, and Transit routes must be generated. The final visible state of the application must be the Drive route for Current location to Meta Headquarters via Stanford University.

windows.openphotoedit1.community_four_ex.instruction:
Produce four edited image files in the photo editing application by importing, adjusting, and saving the specified community photos from the Pictures folder.

The first output, “pe1_orange_buckets_duo-edited.png”, is derived from “pe1_orange_buckets_duo.png”, which shows two smiling women standing side by side in a courtyard, each carrying a large bright orange bucket. This file must reflect basic settings with Temperature at 3, Exposure at 6, Brightness at 4, Contrast at 8, and Saturation at 6; the “Clean” filter preset applied with a Strength of 38; HSL adjustments with Orange at 10 and Green at -8; and Scene adjustments with Structure at 7, HDR at 6, and Warm Sun at 4.

The second output, “pe1_blue_bowl_group-edited.png”, is derived from “pe1_blue_bowl_group.png”, which depicts five volunteers gathered around a prominent large blue bowl under a shelter, stirring ingredients together. This file must reflect Scene adjustments with Structure at 14, Foliage at 5, and HDR at 10; Edit adjustments with Brightness at 8 and Contrast at 6; HSL adjustments with Blue at 12 and Cyan at -6; and additional Scene adjustments with Structure at 10, HDR at 8, and Warm Sun at 3.

The third output, “pe1_white_bowl_group-edited.png”, is derived from “pe1_white_bowl_group.png”, which shows five adults seated indoors in conversation with a large white bowl in the center of the table. This file must reflect the “Cream” filter preset applied with a Strength of 32; Edit adjustments with Exposure at 3, Temperature at 5, and Fade at 4; HSL adjustments with Yellow at -7 and Orange at 4; and Scene adjustments with Structure at 8 and Cool Tone at 3.

The fourth output, “pe1_headscarf_selfie-edited.png”, is derived from “pe1_headscarf_selfie.png”, which features a woman wearing a colorful headscarf in the foreground taking a smiling selfie with three companions behind her who are wearing blue lanyards. This file must reflect Portrait adjustments with Smooth at 8, Whiten at 4, Rosy at 5, Bright Eyes at 6, and Background Blur at 7; Edit adjustments with Saturation at 5, Sharpen at 7, Vignette at 5, Brightness at 3, Temperature at 2, and Fade at 3; and the “Portrait” filter preset applied with a Strength of 24.

Upon completion, the application must remain on the editing page for the “pe1_headscarf_selfie.png” image.

windows.openphotoedit2.experimental_four.instruction:
Produce four edited image exports in the photo editing application, each derived from a specific source file in the Pictures folder and saved with a designated filename.

The first export, "pe2_clown_white_red_tilt-edited.png", is created from "pe2_clown_white_red_tilt.png", which depicts a stage character with a tilted head, white face paint with red triangular markings, and black clothing against a black background. This image must have the "Film" filter preset applied with a Strength of 46. The Edit panel settings for this image are Exposure 7, Contrast 16, Saturation -5, Fade 8, Grain 11, and Vignette 15. The HSL panel settings are Red 9 and Orange -6. The Scene panel settings are Structure 8, HDR 6, and Cool Tone 4.

The second export, "pe2_clown_blue_red_cards-edited.png", is created from "pe2_clown_blue_red_cards.png", which shows a character with a face split into blue and red halves, wearing a black suit and holding a fan of playing cards. The HSL panel settings for this image are Blue 11, Red 8, and Cyan -7. The Edit panel settings are Brightness 6, Contrast 13, Sharpen 12, Exposure 3, Fade 3, and Vignette 4. The "Clean" filter preset is applied with a Strength of 34.

The third export, "pe2_white_contour_profile-edited.png", is created from "pe2_white_contour_profile.png", which features a glowing white line outlining a left-facing profile and shoulder against a pure black background. This image must have the "Night" filter preset applied with a Strength of 52. The Edit panel settings are Exposure -9, Contrast 18, Fade 5, and Vignette 12. The Scene panel settings are Cool Tone 14, HDR 9, and Structure 11.

The fourth export, "pe2_suits_yellow_pink_split-edited.png", is created from "pe2_suits_yellow_pink_split.png", which displays two men in black suits and white shirts talking face-to-face against a background split yellow on the left and pink on the right. The Edit panel settings are Exposure 2, Contrast 10, Saturation -9, and Temperature -4. The HSL panel settings are Yellow -12, Magenta -8, and Orange 5. The Scene panel settings are Structure 9 and HDR 7. The "Film" filter preset is applied with a Strength of 28.

At completion, all four files must be downloaded with their exact specified filenames, and the application must remain on the editing page for the "pe2_suits_yellow_pink_split.png" image.

windows.openphotoedit3.four_exact_export.instruction: Import four specific images from the Pictures folder into the photo editor, apply the designated adjustment sequences to each, and export the results as four distinct files. The first image, identified by the filename pe3_forest_longhair_portrait.png and depicting a woman with long brown hair facing the camera in a khaki jacket within a green forest, must be edited with Smooth set to 7, Whiten to 3, Rosy to 4, Bright Eyes to 6, and Background Blur to 9 in the Portrait tab; Green set to -10 and Yellow to -5 in the HSL tab; Exposure set to 4, Contrast to 6, and Sharpen to 7 in the Edit tab; and the Portrait preset selected with a Strength of 22 in the Filters tab, then downloaded as pe3_forest_longhair_portrait-edited.png. The second image, identified by the filename pe3_concrete_shortcurl_portrait.png and depicting a woman with short black curly hair standing in front of a gray concrete wall, wearing a white sleeveless top and looking to the side, must be edited with Exposure set to 2, Brightness to 5, Temperature to -4, and Sharpen to 9 in the Edit tab; Smooth set to 5, Slim Face to 3, and Bright Eyes to 5 in the Portrait tab; the Cream preset selected with a Strength of 18 in the Filters tab; and Orange set to -5 and Red to 3 in the HSL tab, then downloaded as pe3_concrete_shortcurl_portrait-edited.png. The third image, identified by the filename pe3_forest_waterfall.png and depicting a multi-tiered white waterfall flowing over dark rocks and moss in a dense green forest, must be edited with Structure set to 16, Foliage to 9, Cool Tone to 7, and HDR to 12 in the Scene tab; Green set to -8, Cyan to 6, and Blue to 4 in the HSL tab; Brightness set to 6, Contrast to 8, and Sharpen to 10 in the Edit tab; and the Clean preset selected with a Strength of 30 in the Filters tab, then downloaded as pe3_forest_waterfall-edited.png. The fourth image, identified by the filename pe3_snow_lake_mountain.png and depicting a twin-peaked snow mountain under a golden sunset, with a deep green forest and a complete reflection in a lake, must be edited with Sky set to 13, Structure to 12, Foliage to 5, Warm Sun to 10, and HDR to 11 in the Scene tab; Yellow set to -8, Green to -9, and Blue to 5 in the HSL tab; and Saturation set to -7 and Contrast to -4 in the Edit tab, then downloaded as pe3_snow_lake_mountain-edited.png.
